sentence: This project compares what mesenchymal stromal cells release in normal conditions and in conditions simulating Parkinson’s disease to find molecules that target a protein.
This project studies how genetic variants change gene activity in the cells of mouse tissues and how they affect inflammation.
This project builds mouse epigenome resources and computational tools to find out how DNA methylation affects gene expression and cell behavior.
This project uses machine learning on electronic health record, physiological waveform and genomic data to predict major complications after surgery.
This project looks for biomarkers of drug-resistant multiple myeloma cells in primary human samples and aims to prevent relapse.
This project tests whether dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI can measure how breast cancer responds to chemotherapy in a multicenter study.
This project studies the structure and function of fibrillar adhesins, proteins that bacteria use in infection.
This project studies how alcohol dependence changes activity in a brain reward pathway of mice and drives escalated alcohol self-administration.
This project provides exposure measurement and geospatial modeling methods and tools to support environmental health research.
This project studies how reactive oxygen species and calcium link a mitochondrial pore to the cellular stress response in a nematode.
This project identifies and measures neuropeptides involved in feeding in a crustacean model system, using computational software and an isobaric tagging strategy.
This project studies how cell metabolism and immune function interact and how this relates to cancer and cancer therapy.
This project studies how tissue stiffening and metabolism are linked in pulmonary fibrosis, using patient derived cell lines and animal models.
This project studies how lipid nanoparticle formulation properties affect interactions with blood cells and proteins to build predictive models.
This project provides computational analysis of single-cell transcriptomic, spatial transcriptomic, epigenetic and genetic data to study autoimmune diseases.
This project tests whether connectivity in cerebellar-cortical circuitry can predict how patients with psychosis respond to treatment.
This project develops mass spectrometry technologies to analyze single cells beyond the global proteome, including post-translational modifications.
This project provides statistical and data science support, including study design and bioinformatics, for environmental health research.
This project studies how cells in the bone marrow niche shape leukocyte oversupply and inflammation in mice with cardiovascular disease.
This project studies how alcohol-induced changes to a lipid transporter affect breast cancer progression.
